hard_locks.rationale: Prevents outdated DSL usage and agent hallucinations.
hard_locks.statement: Ash 3.x only. No Ash 2.x APIs/patterns. If uncertain, verify against current Ash docs.

hard_locks.rationale: Ash 3 centers on domains as the resource boundary and configuration hub.
hard_locks.statement: Domain-first architecture: use Ash.Domain as the interaction boundary; do not design around deprecated API boundaries.

hard_locks.rationale: Time-ordered IDs improve indexing and operational ergonomics.
hard_locks.statement: UUIDv7 is the default primary key strategy: use uuid_v7_primary_key and Ash.UUIDv7.generate/0.

hard_locks.rationale: Avoid cross-tenant data leakage and accidental global reads/writes.
hard_locks.statement: Tenancy is mandatory for tenant-scoped data: global? must be false unless explicitly justified and approved in TEN-1.
Authorization is mandatory: all externally-triggerable actions must be authorize?: true and governed by explicit policies/filters.
No anonymous logic in resources: all changes/validations/policy checks must be named modules or named helpers.

notes: scan_max_offline_age_seconds default is 6 hours (21600). Occurrences MAY override within EVT-2 constraints (0..604800).
scan_stale_behavior default is deny (fail-closed). accept_provisional MUST be explicit per occurrence.
Dispute-risk defaults are validate_only to preserve fail-closed posture under uncertainty.
hard_locks.rationale: Prevents silent drift between services and scanners; ensures offline posture and re-entry behavior are consistent even when event data is partially configured.
hard_locks.statement: Suite-wide scanning policy defaults MUST be deterministic. If an EVT-2 Occurrence omits any scan_* policy attributes, the platform MUST apply the defaults defined in GOV-0 (no implicit code defaults).

hard_locks.rationale: Eliminates split-brain between scanner configuration and event policy; ensures staleness evaluation is occurrence-scoped and consistent across devices.
hard_locks.statement: SCAN-1 configured_max_manifest_age_seconds MUST be sourced from EVT-2 Occurrence.scan_max_offline_age_seconds for the same org_id and occurrence_id. No other source is permitted.

hard_locks.rationale: Prevents the offline-accept → online-revoke/refund → organizer-paid fraud path. Forces reconciliation before settlement.
hard_locks.statement: If EVT-2 Occurrence.scan_stale_behavior == accept_provisional, scanners MUST mark the scan decision provisional=true and PAY-4 payout eligibility MUST be held until reconciliation completes (no payout on provisional acceptance).

hard_locks.rationale: Prevents CI theatre and fake confidence from contributor-local or selectively retried proof surfaces.
hard_locks.statement: Protected-branch correctness proof MUST come from blocking CI jobs that execute the normative entrypoints under the pinned toolchain. continue-on-error downgrades, rerun-until-green behavior, and contributor-local variants MUST NOT be represented as release proof.

hard_locks.rationale: Prevents selective proof drift where committed focus/only shortcuts quietly shrink the blocking surface.
hard_locks.statement: Committed focus/only selection is forbidden in the blocking proof surface. Focus tags, only-style shortcuts, and committed mix test --only/--exclude release shortcuts MUST NOT control protected-branch proof.

hard_locks.rationale: Prevents silent burial of flaky or failing tests and makes suppression visible debt with an owner and expiry.
hard_locks.statement: Temporary skipping or quarantine of a blocking test MUST be explicitly governed by a quarantine registry entry carrying issue_ref, owner, expiry_utc, scope, and compensating_control. Indefinite suppression is forbidden.

hard_locks.rationale: Preserves reproducibility and keeps blocking tests from depending on ambient state that cannot be replayed.
hard_locks.statement: Blocking tests MUST be deterministic. Failing seeds MUST be surfaced, and ambient wall-clock or live-network dependence MUST be frozen, injected, or faked unless a downstream contract explicitly governs a separate non-blocking lane.

interpretation.conflict_policy: If GOV-0 conflicts with SEC-1/TEN-1/DP-1/ERR-1/API-0, GOV-0 yields. Fix GOV-0 via version bump + gates.

definitions.admin_approval: An authorized admin approves execution scope; approval MUST be logged and MUST precede execution.
definitions.dual_control: Two distinct approving actors are required for high-risk operations; MAY be enabled by downstream contracts.
definitions.support_validation: A support actor checks verification_evidence completeness and scope correctness; support_validation does NOT execute the operation.

privacy_sensitive_operations_governance.description: Governance framework for operations that access, export, or destroy linkability to subject identity. This framework is referenced by DSAR-1 and PII-1 but is defined here to prevent drift across domains.

invariants.statement: All privacy_sensitive_operations SHALL be capability-gated via IAM-1 and SHALL emit append-only audit records (who, when, capability, reason, scope, outcome).
Any operation that can increase identifiability (PII access/export) SHALL require an explicit, bounded audit reason and verification evidence where applicable.
Any operation that can destroy linkability (cryptoshred / erasure execution) SHALL preserve immutable truth and SHALL record execution evidence (job_id, started_at, completed_at, result, errors).

Break-glass access SHALL NOT be the default. Break-glass SHALL require step-up authentication, a bounded reason, and enhanced monitoring. Break-glass SHALL be subject to post-facto review within a fixed review_window_days.

verification_evidence_requirements.statement: If a flow requires subject verification, verification_evidence SHALL be present and SHALL use allowed_evidence_types. Missing/invalid evidence SHALL block execution.
